ruleset_fingerprints.visibility_note: Two fingerprints, one ruleset, two viewers. runtime_app_visible (903f…) is what the verifier/reviewer GitHub Apps compute over kleinperkins-merge-safety, because GitHub App installation tokens REDACT bypass_actors — the Apps literally cannot see the admin bypass, so their view (and the fingerprint the controller pins for them) is bypass-free and UNCHANGED by the D3 (2026-07-30) admin-bypass bake-in. operator_full (4ff6…) is the owner/admin view, which DOES include bypass_actors and is what merge-safety.ruleset.json.tmpl now renders + `verify-control-plane` recomputes and asserts. The owner attests the operator_full layer separately since app tokens cannot see it.
ruleset_fingerprints.home_merge_safety_bypass_note: D3 (2026-07-30) — PERMANENT FLEET-WIDE ADMIN BYPASS (reverses the prior zero-bypass invariant). Every pr-controlled target's kleinperkins-merge-safety ruleset now grants RepositoryRole admin (actor_id 5) a bypass_mode:pull_request bypass (baked into merge-safety.ruleset.json.tmpl, so newly-activated repos inherit it and the reconcile verb self-heals it), giving current_user_can_bypass=pull_requests_only for the repo owner. Rationale: a governed PR touching protected paths (.github/CODEOWNERS/_ops) is BLOCKED whenever the local controller is paused/offline and cannot post the required `pr-automation / verify` Check; the admin pull_request bypass is the break-glass path (`gh pr merge --squash --admin`) so the solo owner is never permanently locked out — the exact analog of the history-integrity ruleset's admin bypass (§6, _ops/baseline/README.md). Controller-safe: GitHub App installation tokens REDACT bypass_actors, so the verifier/reviewer Apps never observe this bypass and the app-visible ruleset fingerprint they enforce/attest (runtime_app_visible, 903f…) is unchanged — only the owner-visible operator_full layer changes. Proven safe in production: KleinPerkins/pr-automation-controller (the controller's own home repo, merge-safety id 18817498) has run with exactly this bypass live for a while with no App-side impact. It never weakens any real protection: deletion, non_fast_forward, linear history, resolved-conversation, squash-only, and the required Check rules are all untouched.
